paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Probing accuracy with reduced training data.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates probing accuracy as a function of reduced training data size for two multilingual BERT-family models. The x-axis is labeled “Train size,” uses a linear scale, and spans from about 100 to 2000, with regularly spaced tick labels every 250 (250, 500, 750, …, 2000). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 80 to 94 with tick marks every 2 units. Two solid lines with “x” markers are shown: the mBERT series is light blue and increases from roughly 83 at train size ~100 to about 90.4 at 2000, rising quickly early (e.g., ~85.8 at ~200 and ~88.0 at ~500) and then changing more gradually as it approaches ~90–90.4 from ~1500 onward. The XLM-R series is a darker blue and also increases across the x-axis, starting around 84.8 at train size ~100 and reaching about 91.7–91.8 at 2000, with values near ~87.5 at ~200, ~89.6 at ~500, ~90.9 at ~1000, and then a flatter progression around ~91.5–91.8 from roughly 1500 to 2000.
